chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, all together from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah and Abū Baṣīr, who said:

We said to him: A man doubts frequently in his salat (prayer), to the point that he does not know how much he has prayed or what remains upon him. He said: He repeats it. We said: That happens to him often; whenever he repeats, he doubts again. He said: He should proceed despite his doubt. Then he said: Do not accustom the wicked one from among yourselves to breaking the salat (prayer), lest you make him hopeful; indeed al-Shayṭān is wicked and becomes accustomed to what he is accustomed to. So let one of you proceed in the uncertainty and not frequently break the salat (prayer), for if he does that three times, the doubt will not return to him.
Zurārah said: And he said: He only wants to be obeyed, so when he is disobeyed, he does not return to any one of you.

key_terms.الشَّكُّ: doubt regarding the performance of the prayer
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانَ: Satan, presented here as the source of recurring disruptive doubt
key_terms.الْوَهْمِ: uncertainty or misgiving occurring in the prayer
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the act of ritual worship being discussed
key_terms.نَقْضِ الصَّلَاةِ: breaking or invalidating the salat (prayer) by restarting it
key_terms.يَمْضِي: he continues on and proceeds without stopping

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they frequently doubt the number of rakʿahs in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses repeated doubt in salat (prayer), teaching that when such doubt becomes frequent, one should not keep breaking and repeating the prayer. It frames persistent misgivings as a tactic of al-Shayṭān, and instructs the believer to continue the prayer so that the pattern of obsessive doubt is cut off.
